evals.query: Write a Kora 2.0 Kotlin component test for UserService using the application graph. The test should get a real UserService and assert that createUser returns a user.
expected_behavior: Annotates the test class with @KoraAppTest(Application::class) imported from io.koraframework.test.extension.junit5
Injects UserService with @TestComponent on a lateinit var
Adds testImplementation("io.koraframework:test-junit5") and ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}"), versioned through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform
Writes a plain synchronous @Test method — no runTest, no suspend
Does not construct UserService manually or reach into the graph by reflection instead of @TestComponent
anti_behavior: Imports ru.tinkoff.kora.test.extension.junit5.*
Declares the artifact ru.tinkoff.kora:test-junit5 or the BOM ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent
Adds kspTest although the test declares no @KoraApp of its own
Wraps the assertions in runTest { } or runBlocking { }

evals.query: Test OrderService which depends on UserRepository in a Kora 2.0 Kotlin service. Mock the repository with MockK and verify the interaction.
expected_behavior: Combines @field:MockK with @TestComponent on a lateinit var so the mock replaces the graph node
Explains that bare @MockK annotates the Kotlin property and is only discovered when kotlin-reflect is on the test classpath, so @field:MockK is the safe form
Stubs with every { ... } returns ... and verifies with verify { ... }
Declares testImplementation("io.mockk:mockk:1.14.11")
Does not add a = mockk() initializer next to the annotated field
Does not attach @ExtendWith(MockKExtension::class) alongside @KoraAppTest
anti_behavior: Uses coEvery/coVerify for the repository call
Pins io.mockk:mockk at a 1.13.x version
Suggests -Dnet.bytebuddy.experimental=true as the fix for a Byte Buddy class-file error

evals.query: I am migrating this Kora Kotlin test to 2.0. It reads: @Test fun createUser() = runTest { coEvery { userRepository.save(any()) } returns "1"; val r = userService.createUser(req); coVerify { userRepository.save(any()) } }. UserRepository is a Kora @Repository. What should it look like now?
expected_behavior: States that Kora 2.0 repository/controller/HTTP-client contracts are synchronous, so UserRepository.save no longer suspends
Rewrites the test as a plain @Test with no runTest wrapper
Replaces coEvery with every and coVerify with verify
Keeps every original assertion — the migration removes the coroutine scaffolding, not the checks

Warns that a leftover coEvery/coVerify still compiles once the contract stops suspending, because the block is a suspend lambda that may call ordinary blocking functions, so the migration has to be driven by a grep rather than by build errors
anti_behavior: Keeps runTest, runBlocking or a TestDispatcher around the Kora call
Keeps coEvery/coVerify against the Kora repository
Wraps the repository call in withContext(Dispatchers.IO)
Drops an assertion to make the rewrite simpler

evals.query: My Kora 1.x Kotlin suite has a test that launches a coroutine calling a suspend @Repository query, cancels it, and asserts the query was cancelled. How do I port that to Kora 2.0?
expected_behavior: States plainly that this scenario has no Kora 2.0 equivalent: repository methods are ordinary blocking calls on virtual threads and there is no cancellable suspend contract
Recommends deleting the test and recording why, rather than leaving a weakened assertion behind
Offers the nearest surviving intent where one exists — a @Timeout resilience aspect configured through a resilient block in KoraConfigModification, asserted on the exception it throws
Mentions that Flow-returning repositories are likewise gone, so tests collecting one are deleted too
anti_behavior: Invents a Kora 2.0 cancellation API
Silently drops the test without saying the scenario disappeared
Keeps the test but replaces the assertion with something trivially true
Claims Kora 2.0 repositories can still return Flow or suspend

evals.query: After moving my Kotlin service to Kora 2.0 the tests fail with 'InliningClassTransformer - Failed to transform class ... Java 25 (69) is not supported' and then 'Application graph failed to initialize'. My build has io.mockk:mockk:1.13.11. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies MockK 1.13.x as the cause: it carries a Byte Buddy that cannot read Java 25 (class file 69) bytecode, which Kora 2.0 artifacts are compiled to
Raises MockK to 1.14.11 — the version in the Kora 2.0 catalog and the pin used by the migrated kora-kotlin-crud example (1.14.9 is the stated minimum)
Notes the failure is at runtime and hides inside the graph-initialization error with no visible suppressed exception
Suggests ./gradlew <module>:dependencyInsight --dependency byte-buddy --configuration testRuntimeClasspath to confirm what resolved
If mockito-kotlin is also present, pins mockito-core explicitly next to it because mockito-kotlin drags in an older mockito-core
anti_behavior: Recommends -Dnet.bytebuddy.experimental=true as the fix
Suggests lowering the JVM toolchain below 25
Blames the Kora annotation processor or a stale build cache without checking the mocking engine

evals.query: A migration script removed kspTest from all my Kotlin modules. Now one module fails with 'Cannot find generated Kora application graph for: com.example.TestApplication'. Which modules actually need kspTest and which do not?
expected_behavior: States the rule: kspTest("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}") is required exactly when the module's src/test declares its own @KoraApp interface
Points out that an ordinary @KoraAppTest(Application::class) test against a graph compiled in src/main does not need kspTest
Warns that @KoraAppTest is not @KoraApp — searching for @KoraApp must not match @KoraAppTest
Adds ksp { arg("kora.app.submodule.enabled", "true") } to the module that compiles the production @KoraApp being extended, which may be a different Gradle project than the one carrying kspTest
Notes that the extension's own error message spells out both halves of the fix
anti_behavior: Adds kspTest to every module as a blanket fix
Removes kspTest from a module whose src/test really does declare a @KoraApp
Puts kora.app.submodule.enabled on the test module instead of the module owning the production @KoraApp
Claims only one example module in the corpus needs kspTest

evals.query: Set up build.gradle.kts for a Kotlin Kora 2.0 module with @KoraAppTest tests. I copied a koraBom configuration with extendsFrom from our Java module — is that right?
expected_behavior: Says no: Kotlin modules do not create a koraBom configuration with extendsFrom
Applies the BOM directly: implementation(platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:${property("koraVersion")}"))
Gives the processor an explicit version: ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}")
Declares testImplementation(platform("org.junit:junit-bom:${property("junitVersion")}")) with junitVersion=6.1.3 and testImplementation("io.koraframework:test-junit5")
Sets koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 in gradle.properties, resolved from mavenCentral()
anti_behavior: Creates a koraBom configuration and wires it with extendsFrom in a Kotlin build script
Uses ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent as the BOM
Leaves the ksp/kspTest coordinate without a version and relies on the BOM to supply it
Pins 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT or 2.0.0.alpha6 as the version for a new project

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 Kotlin test needs to point the database config at a local PostgreSQL by substituting POSTGRES_JDBC_URL, POSTGRES_USER and POSTGRES_PASS. How do I override config in the test?
expected_behavior: Implements KoraAppTestConfigModifier on the test class body and overrides config()
Returns KoraConfigModification.ofSystemProperty(...).withSystemProperty(...) so the ${VAR} placeholders in the application config resolve
Explains the difference between ofSystemProperty (properties only, config file kept) and ofString/ofResourceFile (the application config is replaced)
Notes the modifier cannot be combined with constructor @TestComponent injection — the extension fails with 'Cannot use KoraAppTestConfigModifier with @KoraAppTest constructor injection'
Uses the 2.0 jdbc section name if any HOCON is written out
anti_behavior: Writes a db { } section
Passes the modifier through the test constructor
Hardcodes credentials into application.conf or bypasses KoraConfigModification with a custom property source

evals.query:
Review this Kora Kotlin test config for 2.0: override fun config() = KoraConfigModification.ofString("""db { jdbcUrl = ... }
publicApiHttpPort = 8081
privateApiHttpPort = 8082
resilient.circuitbreaker.pet { slidingWindowSize = 10 }""")
expected_behavior: Renames db { } to jdbc { }, citing the symptom ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null at path: 'ROOT.jdbc.username'
Renames publicApiHttpPort to httpServer.port and privateApiHttpPort to httpServer.system.port

Explains that the stale port keys are simply unknown HOCON keys — ignored without a warning, so each server falls back to its own default: 8080 for the public server and 8085 for the system server, which SystemHttpServerConfig overrides

Replaces slidingWindowSize with countBased.windowSize and states that omitting countBased fails graph init with IllegalArgumentException: CircuitBreaker 'pet' property 'countBased' is not configured, because KoraCircuitBreaker validates the @Nullable field on construction
Points out that HOCON embedded in an ofString block is invisible to scanners that only read .conf/.yaml, which is why these keys survive migration there
anti_behavior: Repeats the stale claim that both servers bind 8080 and the app dies with 'Address already in use'
Leaves db { } in place
Leaves the circuit-breaker block without countBased
Claims that omitting countBased raises a NullPointerException during graph init
Treats the embedded HOCON as test-only text that does not need migrating

evals.query: In a Kora 2.0 Kotlin test I need to add a Supplier<Int> that is not declared in the @KoraApp, and also replace an existing Supplier<Int> deriving the new value from the original. How?
expected_behavior: Implements KoraAppTestGraphModifier on the class body and overrides graph()

Uses KoraGraphModification.create().addComponent(TypeRef.of(Supplier::class.java, Int::class.java), Supplier { ... }) with the explicit Supplier SAM constructor, because addComponent is overloaded on Supplier and Function<KoraAppGraph, T>
Uses replaceComponent(TypeRef.of(...)) { graph -> ... } and unwraps graph.getFirst(...) with requireNotNull, since the extension package is @NullMarked and getFirst is @Nullable
Passes any tag as a single Class<*> in the second argument position, not as a list
Notes that only the Function<KoraAppGraph, T> overload keeps the replaced node's dependencies; the Supplier overloads and every mockComponent overload drop them
anti_behavior: Passes a list of tags to replaceComponent
Casts graph.getFirst(...) straight to a non-null type without a null check
Registers the component through a factory method on the production @KoraApp instead of the test graph modifier
Supplies the modifier through the test constructor

evals.query: Write a Kora 2.0 Kotlin integration test for UserRepository against a real PostgreSQL via Testcontainers with Flyway migrations.
expected_behavior: Annotates with @Testcontainers and declares a @Container @JvmStatic PostgreSQLContainer in a companion object
Implements KoraAppTestConfigModifier and feeds the container's jdbcUrl/username/password through KoraConfigModification.ofString plus withSystemProperty
Writes a jdbc { } section, not db { }
Declares org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter:1.21.4 and org.testcontainers:postgresql:1.21.4, the coordinates the migrated Kotlin examples use
Adds org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql alongside io.koraframework:database-flyway, since database-flyway ships flyway-core only
Injects the repository or service with @TestComponent
anti_behavior: Writes a db { } section inside ofString
Aligns the org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter version to the JUnit BOM (6.1.3)
Declares org.testcontainers:postgresql at a 2.0.x version — in Testcontainers 2.x that module is named testcontainers-postgresql
Mocks the database or substitutes an in-memory stub for the real JDBC connection
Makes the container an instance field so it restarts for every test method

evals.query: Kora 2.0's version catalog lists Testcontainers 2.0.5. Should I bump my Kotlin test module to org.testcontainers:postgresql:2.0.5 and org.testcontainers:kafka:2.0.5?
expected_behavior: Says those coordinates do not exist at 2.x: Testcontainers 2.x renamed the modules to testcontainers-postgresql, testcontainers-kafka and testcontainers-cassandra
Explains that 2.0.5 is what the Kora framework's own internal, unpublished test fixtures use — every migrated Kotlin example and guide uses 1.21.4 with the classic module names
Recommends starting from 1.21.4 to match the examples, and applying the renames deliberately if moving to 2.x
Notes that org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter has its own version line, independent of the JUnit BOM
anti_behavior: Presents org.testcontainers:postgresql:2.0.5 as a working coordinate
Claims the migrated Kotlin examples already use Testcontainers 2.x
Sets the Testcontainers version from junitVersion

evals.query: I need a test-only repository with deleteAll() and findAll() to clean up between tests in my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service. Set up the TestApplication pattern.
expected_behavior: Declares @KoraApp interface TestApplication : Application with a nested @Repository : JdbcRepository carrying @Query methods
Imports io.koraframework.common.annotation.{KoraApp, Root, Tag} and io.koraframework.database.common.annotation.{Query, Repository} and io.koraframework.database.jdbc.JdbcRepository
Makes the test-only component reachable from a @Root, either through a @Root anchor method or @Root directly on the component, because Kora prunes the graph at compile time
Adds kspTest("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}") to this module and ksp { arg("kora.app.submodule.enabled", "true") } to the module compiling the production @KoraApp
Adds tasks.test { exclude("**/\$*") } so generated $-prefixed classes do not confuse JUnit discovery
Points @KoraAppTest at TestApplication::class rather than the production Application
anti_behavior: Imports ru.tinkoff.kora.common.KoraApp or ru.tinkoff.kora.common.Tag
Omits @Root and expects @TestComponent to find the pruned repository
Puts kora.app.submodule.enabled on the test module when the production @KoraApp lives elsewhere
Skips kspTest even though src/test declares a @KoraApp

evals.query: Our team uses Mockito, not MockK, in a mixed Java/Kotlin codebase on Kora 2.0. How do I mock a Kora component in a Kotlin test with Mockito, and do I need mockito-kotlin?
expected_behavior: Combines @Mock with @TestComponent on a lateinit var and notes that @Mock needs no @field: prefix because it has no Kotlin PROPERTY target
Stubs with Mockito.`when`(...).thenReturn(...) (or whenever from mockito-kotlin) and verifies with Mockito.verify(...)
If mockito-kotlin is added, pins org.mockito:mockito-core explicitly next to it, because mockito-kotlin pulls its own older mockito-core whose Byte Buddy rejects Java 25 class files
Mentions @MockitoStrictness from io.koraframework.test.extension.junit5.mockito and that the default when the annotation is absent is Strictness.WARN
Does not attach @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension::class) alongside @KoraAppTest and does not initialize the field with = mock()
anti_behavior: Adds mockito-kotlin without pinning mockito-core
Claims the default strictness is STRICT_STUBS
Attaches MockitoExtension next to @KoraAppTest
Uses coEvery/coVerify or wraps the assertions in runTest

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 Kotlin test I wrote a fake response mapper: class FakeMapper : HttpServerResponseMapper<Pet> { override fun apply(request: HttpServerRequest, result: Pet): HttpServerResponse { ... } }. The compiler says "'apply' overrides nothing". The identical Java fake compiles. Why?
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause: Kora 2.0 API is @NullMarked with JSpecify, the contract declares the result parameter @Nullable, and Kotlin checks override nullability strictly
Fixes the signature to result: Pet? and unwraps it inside the body with requireNotNull
States the asymmetry explicitly: Java does not enforce this, so a Java test double compiles where its Kotlin twin does not
Notes the error message never mentions nullability, so it reads like a generics mistake
Notes that the same rule applies to KoraAppGraph.getFirst, which is @Nullable and therefore a nullable type in Kotlin
anti_behavior: Suggests annotating the Kotlin parameter with @Nullable or @field:Nullable
Blames the generic parameter or suggests changing HttpServerResponseMapper<Pet> to a raw type
Carries JSpecify or jakarta.annotation nullability annotations into Kotlin sources

evals.query: After migrating our Kotlin Kora module to 2.0, tests run on Linux but a colleague on Windows gets 'CreateProcess error=87, The parameter is incorrect' and the test JVM never starts. The build file has a tasks.test block with environment(["": ""]).
expected_behavior: Identifies the empty environment-variable name as the cause and removes the environment block entirely
Explains that an empty env-var name is not a legal process environment entry on Windows, so the forked test JVM cannot start
Notes this is platform-specific, which is why the same build passes on Linux and CI
Keeps any genuine environment entries the test actually needs
anti_behavior: Replaces the empty key with a placeholder name instead of deleting the block
Blames the JDK toolchain, Gradle version or Testcontainers
Tells the colleague to run tests only on Linux

evals.query: Kotlin, Kora 2.0: after adding `@Component @Conditional(tag = FeatureEnabled::class) class FeatureService` every @KoraAppTest dies at graph init with IllegalArgumentException: Graph node belongs to another application graph (GraphImpl$GraphConditionKey.hashCode). Production startup is fine. How do I fix the test?
expected_behavior: Explains that the extension copy()s the draw (and subgraph()s it for declared roots and mocks), and both keep the original node condition, which reads the original condition node on the derived graph
States it is fixed in 2.0.0.RC2 (kora-projects/kora PR #963), so the fix is upgrading; on RC1 there is no practical workaround besides keeping @Conditional out of the tested graph

Mentions that RC2 also contains kora-projects/kora PR #964, so a PER_CLASS class with MockK or Mockito on the classpath no longer fails in beforeEach on a condition-failed node; on a build with #963 but not #964, PER_METHOD avoids it
anti_behavior: Blames the KSP setup, kora.app.submodule.enabled or MockK configuration
Suggests replacing the conditional component in the test with KoraAppTestGraphModifier as a proven fix
